name: The Ocean Cleanup
scale_note: Over 15,000,000 kg of plastic removed from oceans and rivers as of mid-2024; Interceptors deployed in Guatemala, Malaysia, Jamaica, Indonesia, Thailand, the US and Honduras (org website)

name: Ocean Voyages Institute
scale_note: Over 850,000 pounds of plastic debris retrieved across 10 voyages in the North Pacific Gyre; 340,000-pound haul in 2020 described as the largest open-ocean cleanup in history (org website)

name: Healthy Seas
scale_note: Recovers ghost fishing nets through underwater cleanups at shipwrecks and fish farms, with recovered nets repurposed into products (org website)

name: Ghost Diving
scale_note: Volunteer technical divers removing lost fishing gear; described as a founding partner of Healthy Seas operating cleanup missions globally (Healthy Seas website)

name: Enaleia
scale_note: 2,200,000 kg of marine plastic collected since 2018 with 7,000+ fishers involved daily across Greece, Spain, Italy, Egypt and Croatia (org website)

name: Sungai Watch
scale_note: Team of 180+ river warriors; replicating its Bali model of over 100 river barriers and four sorting facilities into East and West Java (org website)

name: Plastic Fischer
scale_note: Builds and operates low-tech TrashBoom river interception systems with local materials and teams in India and Indonesia (org website)

name: Waterfront Partnership of Baltimore (Mr. Trash Wheel)
scale_note: Four semiautonomous trash wheels operate in Baltimore Harbor since 2014; the original removes 500 tons of litter and debris each year (org website)

name: Greeneration Foundation
scale_note: Citarum River capture system with pyrolysis for low-value waste, aiming to collect 70 tons of waste per day (Clean Currents Coalition)

name: Marea Verde
scale_note: Floating barrier system on the Matias Hernandez River, Panama, with a Mr. Trash Wheel-style upgrade developed with Clearwater Mills (Clean Currents Coalition)

name: Chemolex
scale_note: Plastic capture devices on the Athi River and tributaries, Kenya; average 10 tons collected and converted to construction materials (Clean Currents Coalition)

name: TerraCycle Global Foundation
scale_note: Community-focused plastic capture system on Bangkok's Lat Phrao Canal, Thailand (Clean Currents Coalition)

name: WILDCOAST
scale_note: Binational US-Mexico plastics-intercepting infrastructure on the Tijuana River (Clean Currents Coalition)

name: Renew Oceans
scale_note: Collection of land and river-based plastics on the Assi River (Ganges tributary), India, under the Renew Ganga project (Clean Currents Coalition)

name: The Litterboom Project
scale_note: Over 2.5 million kg of plastic prevented from reaching the ocean across 10 South African rivers, 8 in KwaZulu-Natal and 2 in the Western Cape (org website)

name: everwave
scale_note: 2,634,619 kg of garbage collected from waters using waste collection boats, barriers and cleanups, including missions in Cambodia (org website)

name: Seven Clean Seas
scale_note: River collection, riverine interception, offshore recovery and coastal cleanups in Indonesia and Thailand; targets 8 million kg recovered by its 8th anniversary in 2026 and 100 million kg by 2030 (org website)

name: Ocean Conservancy
scale_note: International Coastal Cleanup has mobilized more than 19 million volunteers and collected over 400 million pounds of trash since the first cleanup in Texas in 1986 (org website)

name: Oceanic Society
scale_note: Global Ocean Cleanup campaign since 2022: 169 cleanups across 140 miles removing 133 tons of waste with 7,725+ volunteers in 14 countries (org website)

name: Trash Hero World
scale_note: Volunteer-led chapter network running community cleanups, with chapters across the world and strong Southeast Asia presence (org website)

name: 4ocean
scale_note: Employs captains and cleanup crews from Florida to Bali cleaning oceans and coastlines seven days a week; each bracelet purchased funds removal of one pound of trash (org website)

name: The SeaCleaners
scale_note: Mobula boats and floating barriers collect waste in Indonesia and Malaysia; Mobula 8.2 collected 2 tons of waste and 135,000 pieces of marine debris in Malaysia in 2025 (org website)

name: Surfrider Foundation
scale_note: Removed 170,000 lbs of trash from US coastlines through 1,230 beach cleanups in 2021 (Impactful Ninja charity directory)

name: Surfers Against Sewage
scale_note: Million Mile Clean: over 19,000 lbs of rubbish removed from UK coastlines by 93,906 volunteers in 2023 (Impactful Ninja charity directory)

name: PADI AWARE Foundation
scale_note: Dive Against Debris program has removed more than 2 million pieces of debris from the ocean with 128,000 diving members (Impactful Ninja charity directory)

name: Olive Ridley Project
scale_note: Cleanups at Hawke's Bay, Pakistan have removed 7,000+ kg of ghost nets, upcycled into consumer goods (Oceanic Society partner page)

name: ARCAS
scale_note: Mangrove and beach cleanups in Chiquimulilla, Guatemala, integrated with community programs (Oceanic Society partner page)

name: Projeto Mar Sem Lixo
scale_note: Community coastal cleanups protecting Rio coastal ecosystems since 2010, translating cleanup data into policy recommendations (Oceanic Society partner page)

name: Keep Bermuda Beautiful
scale_note: 74 cleanups removing 15,000 lbs of waste in 2025; positioned in the North Atlantic Gyre and contributes data to global plastic research (Oceanic Society partner page)

name: SOA Tanzania
scale_note: 2025 cleanup at Mlingotini Island collected 768 kg; establishing a Plastic-Free Coastal Group (Oceanic Society partner page)

name: No Trash Triangle Initiative
scale_note: March 2026 cleanup removed 6.9 tons along 0.6 miles of Bunaken Island; operates an Ocean Plastic Sorting Station ensuring materials are recycled or co-processed (Oceanic Society partner page)

name: Ichthion
scale_note: Azure System combining physical plastic recovery and power generation, deployed on the Portoviejo River, Ecuador (Clean Currents Coalition)

name: Seabin
scale_note: Sydney Harbour program has filtered 36.7 billion litres of water and captured 20.2 million plastic items and 11.1 million microplastics since July 2020 (org website)

name: RanMarine Technology
scale_note: Autonomous WasteShark aquatic drones; 45+ million liters of waste collected since 2016 and 500+ units deployed globally across 4 continents (org website)

name: Clearbot (Open Ocean Engineering)
scale_note: Autonomous electric vessels clean up to 500 kg of surface trash in a single deployment; projects in Hong Kong, India and the Philippines including 4,691 kg collected in Bharatpur (org website)

name: The Great Bubble Barrier
scale_note: Bubble curtains catch plastic from 1mm to 2m across the full width and depth of waterways; installed in Amsterdam, Harlingen, Katwijk, Wervershoof and Vila do Conde, Portugal (org website)
